messages:
maria: Heads-up: Acme escalated — after yesterday's deploy we're seeing p95/p99 spikes on endpoints that use function calling + structured JSON validation. Baseline p95 ~320ms, after deploy p95 ~1.9s and p99 ~4.6s. Customer hitting timeouts. Can eng-runtime help triage?

devin: thx — can you paste a repro (curl) + one trace + any stack-level logs? which model and validation mode are they using?

maria: here's a minimal repro from the customer's payload (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \ \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' \ \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Get order status"}],"function_call":{"name":"get_order","arguments_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"filters":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"k":{"type":"string"},"v":{"type":"string"}}}}}},"output_format":"json_schema"}'
```
Attached is one trace we got from their span collector (trimmed):
```
span: /chat -> router -> validator.compile(schema) [duration: 2200ms]
span: validator.validate -> 1800ms
span: model.response -> 350ms
```
Also noticed worker CPU 90-95% when these requests arrive in bursts.

sam: this looks like schema compilation + validation blocking the request path. If they're sending big nested schemas (arrays of objects), the validator can be expensive. Are we compiling schemas per-request?

devin: checking routing config — the function router currently resolves schema -> compiles validator on first request, but we also hit a code path that invalidates the cache if route metadata changes (we just rolled a small change to tool-routing code yesterday). that could explain cache churn. can you repro switching validation mode to "off" or "async" for that customer to confirm?

maria: did a quick test — toggled validation_mode to "off" for the route (feature-flag via console) for a small sample of traffic. p95 dropped from ~1.9s -> ~330ms and p99 down to ~420ms (still model variance). So validation is the dominant tail contributor.

sam: concrete mitigations:
- cache compiled validators keyed by schema fingerprint and route-config hash (avoid invalidation on unrelated metadata updates)
- precompile schemas at rollout (CI job) for common contracts
- add a fast-path "validator-lite" that does shape checks only for high-QPS routes
- async validation: accept request, return partial/200 with model run and then validate off the critical path (or failover to unvalidated output)

devin: short-term mitigation we can roll in <24h: enable per-tenant validator cache (hotfix) + bump cache TTL, and expose a console toggle to force-disable validation (already did that for Acme). also add sampling to trace validator durations to get better metrics.

maria: customer accepted temporary disable for now (they need reliability). request: can eng-runtime ship the cache hotfix and the sampling change? they want a postmortem + follow-ups.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started hotfix rollout: eng-runtime/validator-cache-fix -> staging at 2026-03-18T03:12Z.

devin: i'll own the hotfix. plan: (1) pin cache key to schema SHA256 + model_variant + small route-config fingerprint (2) skip invalidation on non-schema metadata changes (3) add metrics (histogram of validator.ms) and trace spans emitted for >100ms. rolling to canary in 2h, full prod in 6h if green.

sam: follow-ups for engineering: add a micro-benchmark for worst-case schema shapes (deep nesting, arrays of objects) and optimize validator internal iteration; consider moving to generated validators (ajv compile step) and reusing compiled functions across processes via shared memory or warmup. also validate whether quantization/CPU kernel changes influenced validation CPU cost.

maria: thanks — i've told Acme we'll keep validation off for 48h and share ETA. i'll collect customer logs for the PM/postmortem. pls add the runbook note that validation is an opt-in cost on p95/p99 for structured outputs.

devin: noted, i'll open the PR and the postmortem doc. if anyone sees regressions after the canary ping me: @devin.

maria: one more ask from customer: can we give them a temporary rate-limited "unvalidated" mode for only tool_calls that match a small whitelist? they want to avoid turning it off globally.

sam: we can add per-route validation toggles + allowlist. short term we have the console flag, medium term add per-function metadata and route-level override.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary succeeded: validator-cache-fix -> prod-canary at 2026-03-18T05:40Z (10% traffic). monitoring 30m.

maria: will update Acme and close the escalation if no regressions. thanks team :thumbsup:
